title: How to add CC and BCC in Gmail on Mac: browser steps and keyboard shortcuts
metaTitle: How to add CC and BCC in Gmail on Mac: step by step
description: How to add CC and BCC in Gmail on Mac in your browser: click the links next to To, or use ⌘⇧C and ⌘⇧B after turning on shortcuts.

intro: To add CC and BCC in Gmail on a Mac, open Compose in Safari or Chrome, then click the CC or BCC link next to the To field. You can also press ⌘⇧C for Cc and ⌘⇧B for Bcc, once Gmail keyboard shortcuts are turned on in Settings.
tldr: Open Gmail in Safari or Chrome, then click Compose.
Click CC, BCC or both next to the To field, then type each address.
Use ⌘⇧C for Cc and ⌘⇧B for Bcc after you turn on keyboard shortcuts in Settings.
Cc is visible to everyone on the message. Bcc names stay hidden from the other recipients.
Gmail flags more than 500 total recipients in one email. Google says you can usually send again within 1 to 24 hours.

blocks.text: Gmail on a Mac runs in your web browser. A setup guide from Mailbird, a company that sells a competing mail app, says Google has not released an official Gmail desktop app for Mac. These steps use Safari or Chrome. Apple Mail gets its own section near the end, for people who added a Gmail account there.
What Cc and Bcc do to your recipients

Cc stands for carbon copy. Bcc stands for blind carbon copy. Both send a copy of the message to people who are not the main audience. The difference is visibility. Everyone on the message can see the names in To and Cc. Names in Bcc stay hidden from the other recipients.

Use Cc for people who should see the conversation but do not need to act on it. Google's send-email help says Cc is commonly used that way. Use Bcc when a list of addresses should stay private, such as customers who should not see each other's emails.
Add CC and BCC in Gmail on Mac, step by step
The steps cover the whole flow, from opening Gmail to sending. Step 2 is optional. Skip it if you only plan to click the links and never use the keyboard.

Gmail changes its layout from time to time. The CC and BCC links described here come from Google's help pages and a 2022 walkthrough from How-To Geek. If your screen looks different, look for the same two options next to the To field. The fields work the same way once they appear.
Use keyboard shortcuts for Cc and Bcc

Google's keyboard shortcut table lists Add cc recipients and Add bcc recipients. Google writes the key as ⌘/Ctrl. On a Mac you press ⌘, so Cc is ⌘⇧C and Bcc is ⌘⇧B. The shortcuts do nothing until Keyboard shortcuts are turned on in Gmail settings.

Shortcuts help most when you write a lot of email. Start a new message, press ⌘⇧C, type the first Cc address, and keep typing. Press ⌘⇧B the same way for hidden recipients. Keep your hands on the keyboard and skip the mouse.

blocks.text: A worked example with three kinds of recipients

Say you send a project update. Priya Shah approves the budget, so Priya goes in To. Dan needs the update for records but has no task, so Dan goes in Cc. Forty beta testers should not see each other, so all forty go in Bcc.

Here is what each group sees. Priya and Dan see each other's names in the visible fields. Each beta tester sees Priya and Dan, but not the other testers. The total is 42 addresses, well under the 500 recipient limit in Google's help.
Change a recipient before you send

You can fix a recipient at any point before you click Send. Remove the wrong name from the field, then type the correct address. The message does not leave your outbox until you send it, so this is the safe moment to check.
Mistakes people make with Bcc

Mix-ups happen to careful people. A vendor survey of 1,043 American office workers, collected in October 2023, found that 19.1% had accidentally emailed everyone in their department. EmailTooltester ran that survey. It is not a peer-reviewed study, but it shows how easy a wrong field is to fill.
The most common error is a long list in To or Cc when it belongs in Bcc. Check the three fields before you click Send. Read the names, not just the count. One wrong field can expose a whole list.

Bcc is not a guarantee of privacy in every case. Google's send-email help warns that if recipients do not use Gmail, they may not see that they were added to the Bcc field. If the list is sensitive, tell people they are receiving a copy, or send them a separate message.
Sending limits for large emails

Google's sending limits help says a message can hit a limit if it goes to more than 500 total recipients in a single email. A separate limit applies after more than 500 emails sent in a day. Google says you can usually send again within 1 to 24 hours.
The page does not say whether To, Cc and Bcc count together. Assume they do when you are near 500. Add up every address in all three fields. If the total is high, split the list into smaller sends.
Before you start: check which account you write from

If you use more than one Google account, Gmail opens the one you signed in with. Check the account picture in the top right corner before you add recipients. Sending from the wrong account is an easy mistake, because the compose window looks the same.
Gmail in Apple Mail: the Bcc Address Field

If you added your Gmail account to Apple Mail, the steps change. Apple's Mail guide says that if the field is not listed, you should click the Header Fields button in the message toolbar, then choose Bcc Address Field.
Apple's guide says to leave the To field blank to show Undisclosed-recipients instead of a list of names. Use this when every recipient is in Bcc.

Older guides differ. A 2014 Apple Community reply, written for Yosemite 10.10.1 and Apple Mail 8.1, says to open the View menu and choose BCC Address Field. It also says Command-Option-B toggles the field. That path predates the Header Fields button, so check your own menu first.

Apple's Mail guide has a version selector that lists macOS 27 Golden Gate, macOS Tahoe 26, macOS Sequoia 15 and older releases. The guide does not say which version its steps match. Follow what you see on your Mac.
Checklist before you click Send

items: Check the To, Cc and Bcc rows one at a time.
Put long lists in Bcc, not in To or Cc.
Use Cc only for people who need to follow the thread.
Count every address if the total is near 500.
Tell Bcc recipients who do not use Gmail that they may not notice the copy.

blocks.text: Where to go next

Once Bcc feels natural, turn on Gmail keyboard shortcuts for the rest of your mail. The [keyboard shortcuts guide](/how-to/turn-on-keyboard-shortcuts-in-gmail) covers the settings in full. If a message went to the wrong group, read the [undo send guide](/how-to/undo-send-in-gmail) for Gmail and Apple Mail.

faq.question: Is there an official Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: As far as the sources for this guide show, no. Mailbird's setup guide says Google has not released an official Gmail desktop app for Mac. Use Gmail in Safari or Chrome, or add the account to Apple Mail.

faq.question: Can I add Bcc without showing Cc?
faq.answer: Yes. Click BCC next to the To field and leave the Cc field empty. Gmail shows only the fields you open, so a Bcc row alone is enough.

faq.question: Do Bcc recipients see the other names?
faq.answer: No, names in Bcc are hidden from the other recipients. Google warns that recipients who do not use Gmail may not see that they were added to Bcc, so the copy can go unnoticed.

faq.question: Why do the Cc and Bcc keyboard shortcuts not work?
faq.answer: The shortcuts need Keyboard shortcuts turned on first. Open Settings, then See all settings, then the Settings tab. Select Keyboard shortcuts on and click Save Changes.

faq.question: How many recipients can one Gmail email have?
faq.answer: Google's help says more than 500 total recipients in a single email triggers a limit. It does not say whether To, Cc and Bcc count together, so count all three fields.

faq.question: Does Apple Mail have a shortcut for Bcc?
faq.answer: A 2014 Apple Community reply says Command-Option-B toggles the Bcc field in Apple Mail 8.1 on Yosemite. That reply is old, so test the shortcut on your Mac before you rely on it.

steps.name: Open Gmail in Safari or Chrome
steps.text: Open Safari or Chrome on your Mac. Go to mail.google.com and sign in with your Google account. Gmail opens to your inbox when the sign-in works.

steps.name: Turn on keyboard shortcuts (optional)
steps.text: Skip this step if you only plan to click. For ⌘⇧C and ⌘⇧B, click Settings at the top right, then See all settings. Open the Settings tab, scroll to Keyboard shortcuts, select Keyboard shortcuts on, and click Save Changes.
steps.tip: Reload the Gmail tab after you save so the new shortcuts start working.

steps.name: Click Compose
steps.text: Click Compose to open a new message. Gmail shows the To field first, with the CC and BCC links next to it.

steps.name: Click CC, BCC or both
steps.text: Click CC to add a Cc field, BCC to add a Bcc field, or click both. Use Cc for people who only need to follow the thread.
steps.tip: If you do not see the links, read the layout note in the section above and look near the To field.

steps.name: Type each address in the right field
steps.text: Type the first address in the Cc or Bcc field, then add the next one. Google says you can add recipients in the Cc and Bcc fields. Check the spelling, because a wrong address can still receive the email.

steps.name: Check the To, Cc and Bcc rows
steps.text: Read all three rows once more. Make sure a long list sits in Bcc and not in To. Google warns that recipients who do not use Gmail may not see that they were added to Bcc.

steps.name: Click Send
steps.text: Click Send. Gmail sends the message to every address in all three fields. If it went to the wrong people, use the undo guide linked at the end of this page.
steps.tip: Sending is the last chance to check the rows without help from an undo step.

troubleshooting.problem: I cannot find the CC or BCC links
troubleshooting.fix: Gmail may have changed its layout. Close the compose window, click Compose again, and look right beside the To field. Reload the Gmail tab if the links still do not appear.
Keyboard shortcuts are not on. Open Settings, then See all settings, then the Settings tab. Scroll to Keyboard shortcuts, select Keyboard shortcuts on, click Save Changes, then reload Gmail.

troubleshooting.problem: I added someone to To by mistake
troubleshooting.fix: Remove the name from the To field and check the other rows. If the message already went out, read the undo send guide for the steps that apply.

troubleshooting.problem: Gmail says I hit a sending limit
troubleshooting.fix: Google says you can usually send again within 1 to 24 hours. Wait, then split the list into smaller emails so each one stays below 500 total recipients.

troubleshooting.problem: The Bcc Address Field is missing in Apple Mail
troubleshooting.fix: Click Header Fields in the message toolbar and choose Bcc Address Field. If that button is not there, check the View menu, which older guides describe.
